Channel Memory

Channel Memory#

This example involves a two-operator inclusion problem. Memory effects are present in the communication link to and from evaluation of \(F_1\). The intensity of the memory effects are represented by a scalar \(\alpha > 0\). The network effects are described by a transfer function matrix

\[\begin{split} \mat{c}{z \hdl y} = \mat{cc:cc}{0 & 0 & \frac{\mathbf{z}}{\mathbf{z} +\alpha} I& 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & I \hdl \frac{\mathbf{z}}{\mathbf{z} +\alpha} I& 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & I & 0 & 0} \mat{c}{w \hdl u},\end{split}\]

where \(\mathbf{z}\) is the unit shift operator \(((\mathbf{z} x)_k := x_{k+1}\) for all \(k \in \N\)).

A state-space realization of this transfer function matrix is

\[\begin{split} \text{Network}: \qquad \mat{c}{x_{k+1}^N \hl z_k \hdl y_k} = \mat{cc|cc:cc}{-\alpha I & 0 & \frac{1}{2} I & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -\alpha I & 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}I & 0 \hl 0 & -2\alpha I & 0 & 0 & I & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & I \hdl -2 \alpha I & 0 & I & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & I & 0 & 0} \mat{c}{x_{k}^N \hl w_k \hdl u_k}.\end{split}\]

The degenerate case of \(\alpha=0\) is no network dynamics.

The controller structure with parameters \((\gamma, \lambda) \geq 0\) used to solve the two-operator inclusion problem is

\[\begin{split} \text{Network}: \qquad \mat{c}{x_{k+1}^c \hl u_k^1 \\ u_k^2} = \mat{c|cc}{I & -\gamma \lambda & -\gamma \lambda \frac{1}{\alpha+1} \\ (1+\alpha) I & 0 & 0 \\ I & -\gamma I & -\gamma\frac{1}{\alpha+1} I } \mat{c}{x_{k}^c \hl y_k^1 \\ y_k^2}.\end{split}\]

This controller structure is parameterized by \(\alpha\). If \(\alpha = 0\) and \(\lambda = 1\), then this controller is the same as Projected Gradient Descent. The controller structure is chosen to ensure that the Regulator Equation condition for algorithm convergence is satisfied for all values \((\gamma, \lambda)\). Projected Gradient Descent fails the regulator equation requirement of convergence when \(\alpha > 0\).

We use this algorithm to solve a composite optimization problem

\[\beta^* \in \argmin_{\norm{\beta}_1 \leq 100 } f(\beta)\]

where \(f\) is a convex quadratic with \(m=1\), \(L=5\).

Figure 1 plots a trace of algorithm execution starting from \(x_0 = 0\), highlighting the states of the network and controller.

We now establish tracking properties using the Regulator Equations.

The solution to the Regulator Equations for this network and controller are

\[\begin{split}\begin{align*} \Pi &= \mat{cc}{0 & \frac{1}{2(\alpha+1)}I \\ -\frac{1}{2} I & 0 }, \Gamma &= \mat{cc}{-(\alpha+1) I & 0 \\ -I & 0 }, \\ \Phi &= \mat{cc}{0 & \frac{1}{2(\alpha+1)}I \\ 0 & -I }, \Theta &= \mat{c}{-I & 0}. \end{align*}\end{split}\]

The pair \((\beta^*, w^*)\) solving the composite optimization problem is unique, because \(f\) is strongly convex with a nonempty constraint set is nonempty, and \(f\) is smooth. Algorithm convergence implies tracking of the signals \((x^N, x^c, y, u)\) with

\[\begin{split}\begin{align*} \lim_{k \rightarrow \infty} \mat{c}{x_k^N \\ x^c_k \hl y_k \\u_k} & = \mat{c}{\Pi \\ \Theta \hl \Phi \\ \Gamma} \mat{c}{-\beta^* \\ \nabla f(\beta^*)}. \end{align*}\end{split}\]

Figure 2 plots the tracking of these signals over time

Figure 3 plots the squared norm of the tracking error

Code to generate this simulation is

 1rng(32, 'twister');
 2
 3d = 200; %dimension of variable beta
 4
 5%% describe the operators
 6%define the quadratic
 7m = 1; L = 5;
 8Q = rand_quad(d, m, L);
 9zstar = 100*(2*rand(d, 1) - 1);
10op1 = op_sim_quad(Q, zstar);
11
12%define the L1 ball
13tau = 100;
14op2 = op_sim_l1_hard(tau);
15ops = {op1, op2};
16
17gamma = 0.4;
18lambda = 0.2;
19
20%% describe the network
21%use a transfer function representation 
22%to model the channel memory
23z = tf('z', 1);
24alpha = 0.4; %channel memory effect
25ascale = (2*(alpha+1));
26
27P = [0, 0, z/(z+alpha), 0;
28    0 , 0, 0, 1;
29    z/(z+alpha), 0, 0, 0;
30    0, 1, 0, 0];
31
32%partition the input and output channels
33network = genplant(P);
34network.nw = 2; network.nu = 2;
35network.nz = 2; network.ny = 2;
36
37%% describe the controller
38K = ss([1], [-gamma*lambda, -gamma*lambda/(alpha+1)], ...
39    [1+alpha; 1], [0, 0; -gamma, -gamma/(alpha+1)],1);
40
41
42%% form the system
43sys = opt_system(ops, network, K);
44
45
46%% simulate and plot
47sim = alg_sim(sys, d);
48T = 100;
49sim_out= sim.sim(T);
50plt = alg_plotter(sim_out);
51plt.plot_6(1);
52
53
54%% plot tracking error
55
56%get a more accurate solution to judge tracking error
57sim_out_long= sim.sim(3*T); 
58
59%compute the tracked reference 
60betastar = sim_out_long.z(end, :, end);
61wend = sim_out_long.w(:, :, end);
62dstar = [-betastar; wend(1:end-1, :, end)]; 
63
64
65%compute the regulator equation solution
66reg = regulator_lti(sys);      %solution to open-loop regulator equations
67regcl = reg.check_regulator(); %solution to closed-loop regulator equations
68
69plt = plt.add_opt_sig(regcl, dstar); %compute the error signals
70plt.plot_4_err(2);    %plot the tracking error
71plt.plot_4_sq_err(3); %plot the squared norm of the tracking error
